See also: Influenza

English

[edit]
English Wikipedia has an article on:
influenza
Wikipedia

Etymology

[edit]

From Italian influenza (“influence”), from Latin influentia. Doublet of influence.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˌɪn.fluˈɛn.zə/
  • Audio (US):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɛnzə

Noun

[edit]

influenza (countable and uncountable, plural influenzas or influenze)

  2. (pathology) An acute contagious disease of the upper airways and lungs, caused by a virus, which rapidly spreads around the world in seasonal epidemics.
    • 2020 April 8, Dr David Turner, “How railway staff were conduits and victims of a pandemic”, in Rail, page 32:
      In early 1919 the Board also issued a film, Dr Wise on Influenza, in which a character called 'Brown' spreads the disease by enacting poor behaviours.
      This did address transport - by boarding a crowded omnibus, "Brown may be scattering germs throughout the carriage and giving influenza to a number of people".

Synonyms

[edit]
  • flu
  • grippe, grip

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Italian influenza, from Latin īnfluentia. Doublet of influencia.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /influˈenθa/ [ĩɱ.fluˈẽn̟.θa] (Equatorial Guinea, Spain)
  • IPA(key): /influˈensa/ [ĩɱ.fluˈẽn.sa] (Latin America, Philippines)

  • Rhymes: -ensa (Latin America, Philippines)

Noun

[edit]

influenza f (plural influenzas)

  1. influenza
    Synonym: gripe
    • 2025 June 9, Sarah Owermohle y Meg Tirrell, “RFK Jr. destituye a todos los miembros actuales del comité asesor de vacunas de los CDC”, in CNN en Español‎[1]:
      El comité de los CDC tiene previsto reunirse del 25 al 27 de junio para debatir las vacunas contra el covid-19, el VSR, la influenza, el VPH y la enfermedad meningocócica. El HHS indicó que la reunión se llevará a cabo, lo que le da a la agencia aproximadamente dos semanas para conformar su panel asesor.
      (please add an English translation of this quotation)
